title: PermissionRule
description: One rule that outlives a session, as the client sees it (plan 03; plan 28, B-33; plan 15, B-02). `status` is computed at the moment of the answer, because the list shows an expired rule marked and not missing. The fields below `disabled` are plan 15's additions to the management screen: every one of them is optional here because the routes that fill them in are implemented phase by phase (F1); the normative contract — where each is always present — is `backend/03-modules.md`'s `permission` section, not this flag.

scope.description: The scope of a granted rule. `session` is part of the domain's type but every rule reachable from these routes is `project` or `always`: a `session` rule lives in memory only and is never persisted or listed here.

kind.description: The canonical kind the pattern names — `shell`, `file.edit` —, `null` on a disabled rule.

toolName.description: The kind again, or the engine's pattern of a disabled rule — kept beside for the published app, which reads it (plan 28, D-22).

pattern.description: The pattern exactly as written, in the canonical grammar — or, on a disabled rule, the engine's grammar it was written in.

engine.description: The engine the rule is restricted to, or `null` for every engine whose calls have the kind.

grantedBy.description: Who granted it. Always the caller, since nobody sees another person's rules.

disabled.description: Deprecated in favour of `legacyPattern` and `disabledReason` below (plan 15, D-20 revision): `reason` is an opaque string, not translatable. Kept so the current `PermissionRulesController` keeps compiling until F1 rewires it to the two richer fields.

reason.description: Why the rule was switched off — a rule written in an engine's grammar that had no unambiguous canonical translation.

reach.description: Absent on a rule a route has not been taught to fill yet, and always absent on a `disabled` rule, which has no canonical pattern to describe.

breadth.description: How wide the pattern reaches, by the domain's table per `kind` (plan 15, D-09). Absent on a route that has not been taught to fill it yet, and always absent/`null` on a `disabled` rule.

legacyPattern.description: On a `disabled` rule only: the pattern exactly as it was written, in the engine's own grammar — opaque text, never reparsed (plan 15, D-20 revision). `null`/absent on every other rule.

disabledReason.description: On a `disabled` rule only: why the plan 28 migration could not translate it — translatable, unlike `disabled.reason` above. `null`/absent on every other rule.

findings.description: What the redundancy/overlap/conflict analysis (plan 15, B-15) says about this rule against the caller's other active rules — absent until that route exists.

usage.description: How much this rule has answered, from the trail (plan 15, D-05) — absent until the route that fills it exists.

windowDays.description: The retention window the count is scoped to — 90, today.

grantedVia.description: How the rule came to exist — `null` for a rule granted before this column existed (plan 15, B-07). Absent until the route that fills it exists.

grantedFromRequestId.description: The permission request the card answered, when `grantedVia` is `approval` — `null`/absent otherwise.

templateId.description: The catalog template this rule came from, when it was granted via a template — `null`/absent otherwise.

restoredFrom.description: The revoked rule this one restores, when `grantedVia` is `restore` — `null`/absent otherwise (plan 15, D-11).

folderReachable.description: Whether a `project` rule's folder is still in the caller's allowlist, checked by the pure rule without touching disk — `null`/absent on an `always` rule, and absent until the route that fills it exists.

etag.description: Derived from `expiresAt` and `revokedAt` — there is no version column. What `PATCH /permission-rules/:ruleId` conditions its write on. Absent until the route that fills it exists.

expiryCeiling.description: How far `PATCH /permission-rules/:ruleId` may extend this rule's validity, counted from the moment it was read (plan 15, D-14) — the installation's ceiling for this `decision`, `deny` living longer than `allow` (D-04). `null`/absent on a `disabled` rule, which answers nothing and has no validity to extend. Absent until the route that fills it exists.
